items_missed: 1_set_agenda: Never asked 'How are you today?' and never gave an explicit agenda statement ('here's what we'll cover, sound good?') up front.
2_probe: Didn't ask about packing service needs, storage needs, or moving stressors ('anything you're particularly worried about?').
3_pricing: Never mentioned Meet Your Mover (mover photo/info before the move) or the On-Time Guarantee (discounting if the window is missed).
4_clock: Never stated the 2.5-hour minimum, that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, or an explicit sense-check ('does that make sense?').
5_estimate: Didn't explicitly confirm the number of trucks for this specific job or mention traffic as a possible variable.
6_save_your_ass: No prep speech at all - no mention that prepping before move day shortens the job and lowers the bill, no consolidation examples, no carload tip.
7_quote_booking: Didn't mention the bolded key-details list at the top of the confirmation email or ask the customer to reply with any corrections.
8_politeness: Only used the customer's name ('Susan') once - short of the 3+ times needed; leaned on 'ma'am' instead.
9_bonus: Speech was rambly with a lot of filler ('yeah,' 'okay,' restarted sentences), and the insurance explanation skipped the 60-cent/lb baseline comparison.
top_strength: Landon kept a genuinely messy call organized - a mother calling in for her daughter, mixed-up contact info, two different emails - and still proactively walked through damage coverage, equipment, payment method, deposits, and cancellation policy before being asked, booking the move in under 10 minutes.
coaching_note: Landon runs an efficient, likable call and closed the booking, but he's leaving real points on the table in three specific spots: he skips the Save Your Ass prep speech entirely (0/10, the single biggest miss), he never mentions Meet Your Mover or the On-Time Guarantee in his pricing pitch, and he never states the 2.5-hour minimum or opens with a real agenda statement. Build those three pieces into his call flow as a fixed checklist - each takes under 30 seconds and they're worth real points every call. Also work on using the customer's name more than once; it's an easy fix for the politeness score.
phone_presence_notes: Consistent warmth ('we get it,' 'we totally get it'), patient with a confusing multi-contact situation, and the customer ended the call thanking him twice.
